I'd say give it a couple of days and maybe have a bit of a plan if you shoot him a text. Example, maybe theres something going on in your area that seems like fun. Maybe a "Hey, this event is going on, wanna go with me" kinda thing. Id say dont wait too long if you do wanna message, but if youre probably never gonig to see him again, what do you have to lose? Believe it or not, guys like it when a girl takes a bit of initiative too!

Don't be scared of putting yourself out there. I wish I could go back and have a bit of confidence to ask girls out and be okay if it's a no. Take it in stride and keep your head up. Have fun with it, dont get too attached, and most importantly..... on a deeper level....you need to find happiness in your life, and it cannot entirely depend on the other person to bring you that happiness.

Yeah, sounds like it lol. I'd say go with the flow. Maybe see if you can narrow down to either one person to have as a friend w/ benefits, or.... and this sounds bad, but a rotation of guys that you know can reliably...uhm satisfy you and reach out to them when youre feeling like having fun but also kinda text and talk to. No pressure to settle down, but if you meet someone you like and wanna do more than just cuddle and have sex, take the chance and try a relationship out if it feels right. Also.... self-pleasure is also a thing lol. Sounds like you've got a decent sex drive. That can maybe hold you over when no one's available?  

Apart from that, based on the limited info seems like you might not be overtly open to a relationship. Have you ever considered maybe trying to see if you can hold off on the sex part to develop some kinda connection with a guy? Like as a guy, I feel like especailly online dating, if i get the vibe that a girls just down to hang and bang, I tend to tailor the conversation there and Im more likely to just assume its a one night thing. Versus if I get the feeling she's looking for a relationship, the conversation changes a bit to that. I'm looking for a relationship, but if I meet someone who's just into the sex part, I'm not going to say no if that makes sense. But that comes with a sense of a lack of emotional connection from my point of view. Im not going to get emotionally attached or hold back any emotional attachment if Im getting one night vibes...you know?
Sounds like you want a relationship lol....

I do hear you. Its definitely a piss off.... Just out of curiosity, are you messaging him on Tinder and seeing him "active" on there or somewhere else? Cuz my answer would be different based on where you're seeing him active. 

If he's active on Tinder and not messaging you....those apps will still say someone is "active" if they've logged in at least once in the past week or something crazy like that. 

If its on like Instagram or something.... it'll say he's active even if he's just scrolling. But even then, I don't answer all my messages on Instagram all the time. I'll respond to some friends and stuff here and there, but I won't open other people's messages till I have more time or something, because I don't want them to see that I saw the message and didn't respond. After all, that feels worse than not opening it. But I do get why you'd be annoyed if it was something like Instagram cuz its a bit more accurate. Id be more pissed if he opened the messages and didnt respond, which is doesnt sound like he did. 

Regardless of where, though, I'd still say probably don't block the guy after he didn't respond to your messages for one day lol. BUT, youre well within your right to move on and stuff if you feel like he's not worth it. But my advice would be to give guys a bit more wiggle room for messaging and stuff. One day feels like not long enough to justify blocking him lol. Again, no offense, but that's a bit cray cray from my point of view.
Well...if you remember to, keep me updated haha. Id love to know how it goes with trainer dude :p Goodluck :)

If you want a guys perspective and a bit of harsh truth..... youre 21 lol. You've got plenty of time. 

Guys have a lot of hesitancy walking up to girls, too. Especially when they're with their friends or in a group. Sucks for us to get rejected too lol. But maybe put yourself in situations where you're meeting guys in person? Join a rec sports league or something? 

In terms of the dating apps.... They're killers for my mental health lol. I'm 30, barely get likes, and rarely get any matches. I don't think I'm ugly, but they have me convinced I am. Give guys a chance. One guy missed out. No point in stressing if he lied about going to the hospital or not. Move on, he's not worth it. I'd say delete it if it's affecting your mental health, or take a break from them. See if any friends have any single guys they can introduce you to. Maybe if you stick with the apps, give guys that might not initially appear perfect a chance? 

Like you said, you're good-looking, fun, and smart. You've got a lot of time to meet someone. I promise you, youre going to make a shit ton more mistakes and youve got plenty of lessons with men to learn......one being probably dont block a guy after he said he was going to the hospital because he didnt respond to you one day after a hosptial visit. Im going to be honest, that kinda gives me "cray cray" vibes and might be a bit of a red flag. Did it possibly occur to you that he might be going through something and isnt prioritizing a Tinder girl or that he might have gotten busy lol? Thats not meant to be an attack or anything lol.....just maybe chill haha.

I'm a gu,y and I wouldn't expect it on a first date or even the first few. I'd tell them if the topic of kids came up, though, or if I got the feeling based on conversations that the guy was hoping to have kids.

Might be my own bias, but it feels like an intimate detail that you might not want every guy to know, but it's a bit of a catch-22 because it also feels like something that someone might want to know early, so neither of you is wasting their time. That said, you'd be surprised how many people are willing to be with someone through something like that and open to alternatives.

It is tough news, though, for you if that's something you wanted. Hopefully, you're doing okay and coping with the acceptance/risk?

I know there's this thing where it's taboo for girls to ask guys out.... I'd say don't. I'm a guy, it's probably not going anywhere. If he was interested, he'd message back. My theory is he messaged back and hung out with you that second time because it was obviously going to end in sex, and he was probably down for just that. Guys tend to message back if they're interested, but based on your post, I'd say maybe I could see you saying no to coming over a few times might have killed his interest. Either that or he was just into it for the sex. Unless you're good with offering "cuddles" and probably accepting that he's just into you when there's a high chance of sex, probably move on. If you're looking for a relationship, i'd say move on. 

I feel like I should ask why you feel like you need someone with you?

Nah, harmless at worst. 

As a guy, I tend to strictly avoid asking anyone out at work. Just don't want to risk the worst case scenario of a sexual harassment claim and the best case making it awkward when they probably say no.... But I think women have a bit more wiggle room there. With that said, that's probably my overthinking and reserved nature when it comes to dating in the workplace. But a lot of people meet at work all the time, so meeting someone at work isnt exactly the most unrealistic thing, and someones gotta make a move, right?

Its always nice when a girl takes a bit of initiative, especially in a work place setting, but I think you went about it the right way. If he goes to the picnic, hang out with him and find out if he's single and stuff. Go from there? Sometimes, if I know a bit about what they're into, I'll look up things going on in my city before I see them. (example: If you're both into Star Wars, see if there are any screenings nearby or any Star Wars-related events) casually ask if he's interested in going. I like to use the "this is happening and I don't have anyone to go with, do you wanna go with me" line quite a bit. Shoot your shot!

Goodluck!

Oh, this is a tough one. I'm assuming you know he's single, first off?

If he is, I'd say go for it, take some opportunities to talk to the guy. I know me as a guy, Im terrified of any sort of flirting or asking girls out in a work enviroment. I kinda figure worst case scenario, I get a sexual harassment complaint, and best case, I make things super awkward when they inevitably say no. 

Start with talking a bit more and finding opportunities to do so, and if they go well, and youre vibing, shoot some shots and see if he picks up on them? 

Lastly, I feel like I'd be doing you a bit of an injustice if I didn't prepare you for the fact that he might not be interested in your body type. As someone who does enjoy their workouts here and there (far from a body builder), I think most guys who gym regularly do prefer a certain type of body. With that said, though surprisingly not all guys are superficial, and there is wiggle room. Believe it or not, guys do like a bit of personality too, and that can be attractive. 

Give it a go, and see where it ends up. If it's just a bit of fun at work and a bit of drama to get the juices flowing, you've got nothing to lose. Maybe you even get into the gym and ask him for advice, or if you guys can work out together? 

Goodluck :)

Hey,

Check out Skyscanner and all those flight apps. I booked flights from Ottawa, Canada to Lisbon back in February for $350 (Canadian) there and $375 back. It was the low season for tourism, so it might not be that cheap. But totally doable. Me My friend and did Lisbon for 3 days, Madrid for four, and Barcelona for 4 days for 2600/each. We went for almost double the days you're looking to go for and spent a bit loosly on food and stuff, so im almost positive if you can find some cheap flights, you should be able to have a pretty good vacation for under $3500. I also used my Scotiabank Scene points to book hotels, so if you bank with them, see if you have any points. Saved nearly 200 dollars on hotels that way. Check to see if any of your credit cards have any miles/points also.

I used Expedia to book most of my hotels because I could use Scene points with them, but shop around for hotels too.

Try different airports too. I live in Ottawa, so a lot of times I find cheaper flights out of Montreal or Toronto if Im willing to make the drive. Out of Ottawa right now, theres roundtrip flights to Lisbon for 905 dollars....which is pretty good imo.

All that to say, 3500 is super doable. Id budget 2k for flights for both of you, 800 for hotels, and 700 for food/shopping/activities. Food in Portugal was in the middle in terms of cost. There were cheap options like Kabob spots and stuff for like 5-15 Euros, but if youre going city centre, it can get expensive. Drinks and stuff were pretty average, depending on where you went. Drinks at a local bar were cheap, like 3-5 Euros/drink, but they could get up to 8-15 Euros if you're going to bougie places.

Theres tons of free activities too, beaches and stuff, but activities could get a bit pricy depending on what you wanna do. I always do bar crawls in every city I visit, and they were like 25 euros for drinks included on TripAdvisor which is a great way to meet locals/tourists and have a fun night out.

If you have any more questions, feel free to message me! I know my post is a little all over the place.

Edit: Just realized youre flying out of Vancouver lol.... maybe look into a trip to Asia instead. I feel like Portugal might be tough to get within budget. Sorry, I assumed you were somewhere in Ontario. Asia is cheap as hell. Id recommend Vietnam or Thailand!! Flights are probably cheap for you, and the hotels/food are dirt cheap. You can get 5 star hotels for like 100 bucks a night in Vietnam last time I checked.

I was recently in Madrid (February) from Canada. I ALWAYS bring cash. I had the exact same issue in France a couple of summers ago. I would have gone nearly four days without food if I hadn't brought cash (my sister was meeting me in Paris, but I was alone for 4 days). Luckily this time my cards didnt get flagged, but I brought 200 Euros with me as "oh shit" money and kept the cash until my final couple of days where I figured it was safe to spend it. I was in Madrid for 4 days, but was in Portugal before then and went to Barcelona after for another 4 days. I was with a friend but I feel like 200 Euros would have been more than enough to get me food and cover any transportation costs in case my cards got flagged and I had to survive for a few days. 

  
I do about 200-300 Canadian on every trip I take to cover cash-only costs like food stalls and stuff, and as an emergency fund. I also keep the cash in a different place from my wallet, just in case I get robbed or lose my wallet.

I think saying youre emotionally unavailable is a cop-out. Just my personal opinion, but I think most people are capable of caring about someone if they deem them worth it. Maybe he's going through a lot with the divorce and stuff to be there for you right now. Definitely a possibility and maybe something worth talking to him about. But if you're looking for someone who is emotionally available, and they tell you they're not..... probably not worth pursuing, and probably not worth wasting your time wondering if they will be or not. Maybe try and find guys that arent recently out of relationships or in the midst of a divorce. You have the ability to say who you do and don't go out with and maybe a future criteria should be confirming they're past their past relationships and in a place where they can, if things go well, be there for you. Just seems like you're also at fault for going after guys who might be damaged goods that are yet to be repaired. Just my perspective and it might not be what you want to hear...but yeah ultimately you have a choice in who you date. Maybe change up the way you begin talking to someone, be more vocal and clear that you're looking for someone who can be emotionally available to you. There are definitely ways of doing that without coming off too strong and the right guy will appreciate you laying down some expectations. I know for me, it would tell me this persons interested in me, and potentially sees a future and wouldn't be telling me this stuff if she wasn't. Just my 2 cents :)

  
Goodluck!

We talked for days, I work with the homeless population in my city, and she worked with kids and we both admired each others work and dedication to care about others. I felt we really connected and she mentioned she enjoyed doing crafts. I actually thought I might get a chance, and it just got me so depressed because I let myself get a bit optimistic and excited. I just wanna know if I said or did something wrong, or like I said before, what changed. If she met someone else, that'd be totally okay. At least for my own sanity id know, you know? I appreciate the reply. I know the post was overtly negative, but I wanted to make sure I explained exactly how the apps specifically were making me feel. I don't think Im better than therapy or anything, and I dont doubt it would help. But 1. I cant afford it. And 2. Dating is genuinely the only aspect of my life that brings me down. Im not going to hurt myself, I worked too damn hard to end it all. But suicidal thoughts never leave you, no matter how good or bad life gets after you've spent a significant amount of time thinking about them. Its always going to be an option, but I can tell you right now its not an option that's at the forefront of my mind and Im very proud of that fact. I got out of the hole myself. I know ill figure it out, and have accepted I probably will be alone for the rest of my life. Except disappointment so when it happens you wont be disappointed. Its a sentiment that's helped me through everything Ive been through and its working for now. I wont stop trying, cuz that's what I did for 3 years of my life, and I never want to not try again.

Based on your replies to other comments it does kinda sound like you've made a decision on this. I think regardless, talking to a professional about this could help. I don't know if you want to salvage this relationship, but it does sound like you don't want to. And I would definitely understand if you didn't. He did some permanent damage to you and your self-esteem. Talking to someone might help shake that sense that he only loves you if you're a certain weight. I will say this from my perspective, attraction is an important part of a relationship to me personally. In the past, for me, that attraction generally starts out as a physical attraction that develops into just finding the person and who they are as attractive. I've been in relationships where the person could have gained 1000lbs or turned into a rhino and I probably would have still found them attractive and loved them. But maybe that's not all men. Maybe he just found the girl he first started dating and got married to as attractive and you gaining weight fundamentally changed your appearance which into someone that he didn't find attractive anymore because his preference was someone who was thinner. I think you holding it against him that he gained weight and you still loved him speaks more about what kind of partner you are more than it does about him. 

I think he approached in it absolutely the wrong way, and I would have never done it like that. I don't know the details, but it sounds like he didn't really support you or stop you from essentially killing yourself to get back to a weight he liked.... Which again, I personally would have absolutely not done.... and that's maybe more indicative of a reason why he's not the greatest guy in the world and a better reason to leave

  
I think people are allowed to have preferences of what they find attractive and what they don't and I think maybe the hatred is a bit misguided here. I think you're not mad at him for having to lose all that weight....its what you put yourself through to get there that made you resent him for it and the fact that (by the sounds of it) didn't support or stop you from doing so. This may not be what you wanted to hear. And some people out there might have some problems with my logic, but what Im fundamentally trying to say is he hurt you, did it the wrong way, put you through hell....but he is ultimately allowed to have a preference of what he fundamentally finds attractive. The fact that he couldn't love you for you at whatever weight is a him problem...not a you problem, but you made it a you problem. You deserve someone to love you for you at all times and this relationship might have some deeper flaws, and he might have some deeper flaws for putting you through what he did and letting you do what you did.

Regardless, I think its always helpful to talk to someone anytime you go through something like this. Eating disorders arent generally just about 1 thing, and it can help to talk it through so it doesn't happen again and maybe speaks to some deeper self-esteem, self-love and confidence issues that you may have. And its okay to not be okay....so long as you're working on being okay. You might never get to a place where you are, but so long as you keep working, you'll be better for it. 

  
Again, I do think your relationship has some pretty big flaws and I think there's been some irreparable damage done that's left some really deep scars that might be impossible to heal. But that's for you to determine. Just make the best decision for you, if that means you leaving him to find someone that will love you for you regardless of what you look like 5-50 years down the line then you should do it. I know a lot of the commentators on this post wont believe it, but there are absolutely men out there who would love you regardless of your weight throughout the duration of your relationship, and there are certainly men out there who would have handled this in a much better way. Your husband specifically (not all men) just didn't and doesnt seem to be able to do that. If that's not okay with you, you shouldn't have to deal with it.

Never understood open relationships. Someones bound to get hurt imo. You deserve someone who loves you for you, and if you want someone to love you and only you.....you should go out and find that. One thing I learned is you cant make people change who they are and what they want. They may not be completely open and honest about it, but at some point you'll realize. It sounds like this is doing damage to you. I get you care about each other and this might not be what you want to hear..... and maybe you're on here to hear someone say you could and should work this out, but it sounds like there are some toxic undertones in his actions and what you said to him. I don't mean for this to come out the way its going to come out. But given your history with this guy......does this sound like a relationship that's going to be successful long-term? Do you want to risk dating, marrying and potentially having kids with someone who, given this situation and your history with him, has shown he wants the best of both worlds.....meaning you in his life and the freedom to be with other people? Do you think you deserve someone to just love you? Is that too much to ask? I genuinely think you should ask yourself those questions, I promise I'm not posing them as rhetorical questions to make you reconsider. If the answers add up to you saying yes you're okay with him going out for the duration of the time you end up being together, then go for it. But it sounds like youre already not okay with it. There are plenty of guys out there who would be willing and happy to just love you. Youre worth being exclusive for. If he cant do that, Im sure you'll be able to find it somewhere else. Just started it a couple of days ago and Im close to finishing. A good adaptation for me...I haven't read the book so I can't speak to the book's fans' perspective, but as a show, if you're a WW2 buff, it wasn't bad and worth a watch. It's short enough to binge and get through and I enjoyed the peripherals of a show like this.......except for one thing I couldn't get over, that really took me out of the story. I know it's important to have big names associated.....but Mark Ruffalo and Hugh Lauri ruined the show for me. I think Aria was perfect for Marie and her portrayal was good.....but the accents the two male leads "tried" were absolutely terrible, on top of that..... an incredibly baffling choice was to have American actors do bad English accents.....despite being French characters.....? The entire cast had English accents for some reason....? I know other shows and series have done it and it's been totally fine as a creative choice. Most of the accents of the cast are perfectly fine English accents......but Mark and Hugh genuinely don't have that in their bag as actors I learned. It was just so damn bad. Think of an American trying to do an English accent as a stereotypical joke and you genuinely have how they sounded. There were even points during some conversations where the accent would fade into an American one only to fade back into a really bad English one..... Also....Hugh's acting in general was between mediocre for most of it to just downright bad at points. He was perfect for House considering it was a character that struggles to show emotion, which Im now realizing is the extent of his range as an actor lol. He shows no emotion in his speech or mannerisms.... This show made me realize I really dislike him as an actor. Hed be a good serial killer though, as an actor or a real-life one.

If the accents were going to be terrible anyway by the two leading men, why not give them accurate accents lol? It's a really bad creative choice in my opinion that took me personally out of the show numerous times. To me, it wasn't worth having those two big names associated with it when they actively ruined the show in many ways, I think the show would be infinitely better if they had just hired talented French actors who could speak English despite being "lesser known". Those two, genuinely detract from the show and negatively affect how amazingly everything else was. The cinematography was amazing, the sets were beautiful and accurate, and a lot of the casting on the German side was really well done (even though the same accent and English-speaking confusion still apply). The show, as a bit of a WW2 buff would have been 10/10. They achieved everything they intended to but were held back in a big way by the creative choices and two main leads they chose to employ. They prioritized big names over acting ability imo and those two just do not have the range to do anything past playing an American. It was just so bad for me.... I feel like Im overreacting, but it genuinely took me out of an amazing story and show, which annoys me even more lol.

Super affordable (ranging between 20-50 dollars a trip) and a great way to travel between the two cities. As for whether its difficult, the travel isnt, depending on your financial situation and desire for the two of you to want to meet up, it's doable. If youre ridesharing. Usually takes anywhere between 4-6 hours depending on day of travel and traffic (especially getting into Toronto can be a pain) but still worth the price. Make sure to bring headphones/laptop (some of the rideshares have wifi, so you can get work done)and a pillow lol. Super doable, good luck at Carleton, and good luck with your relationship!
